source_text:
15.34 ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ∆ρᾶσέ τί που καὶ νερτερίοις μετὰ πνεύμασιν ἀνδρῶν
Φεβρωνία ἑῆς σύμβολα συμπαθίης, εἴ τις κἀνθάδε χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν ἦε πένησιν· οὐδὲ

γὰρ οὐδ' αὐτοῦ τῆς σφετέρης ἐς ἅπαν ψυχαὶ λήθονται μεγαθύμων εὐεργείης· ἔμπα γε
μὴν αἰὼν ἡμετέρου βιότου ἄρκιος εἴη θεῖον ἐπὶ προέμεν θάλαμόν μιν Χριστοῦ, τόν
ῥα νυὸν σεμνὸν ἕλ' ἀφθορίης λαμπάδ' ἐλαίῳ φαιδρύνουσα φιλοπτωχείης· ἧς τόδε
σῆμ' ὕπνου γνῶθι πολυχρονίου.

1
thought_title: Febronia's compassion remembered even among the dead
orientation: Arethas, the author, closes with a third epigram praising Febronia's compassion for the poor and her consecration as a bride of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Of the same. Febronia did somewhere also among the nether spirits of men some symbols of her compassion, if there was here any need of the wealthy for the poor; for not even there do the souls of the great-hearted forget their beneficence to the uttermost; yet indeed may the age of our life be sufficient to send her forth to Christ's heavenly bridal chamber, she who took the august lamp of purity as a bride, making it bright with the oil of love for the poor; know this to be her sign of long sleep.

choices.english: among the nether spirits of men
choices.why: Keeps the spatial metaphor of the underworld and the genitive 'of men' explicit, matching the source word order and force.
Renders σύμβολα literally as 'symbols' and keeps the possessive force of ἑῆς with 'her', preserving the idea of tangible tokens of compassion.
Captures the adverbial force of 'to the whole extent', emphasizing the completeness of the dead's memory.
Keeps the optative wish force of εἴη and the adjective 'sufficient' from the glossary sense of adequacy.
Renders the aorist ἕλε as 'took' and keeps the genitive 'of purity' with 'lamp', matching the glossary terms for both.
Renders σῆμα as 'sign' and the genitive phrase as 'of long sleep', preserving the metaphor of death as sleep and the adjective 'long'.

pass_b_english: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, did something with tokens of her compassion, if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor. For not even there do the souls of the great-hearted forget their beneficence to the uttermost. Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on to the divine bridal chamber of Christ—she, as a reverend bride, took hold of the lamp of purity, keeping it bright with the oil of love for the poor. Know that this is the sign of her long sleep.

problems.quote: if here too the wealthy had any need of the poor
problems.source_quote: εἴ τις κἀνθάδε χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν ἦε πένησιν
problems.why: Reverses the relationship: source says 'if there was any need of the wealthy by the poor', not poor needing wealthy.
problems.fix: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy

problems.quote: she who took the holy lamp of purity
problems.source_quote: τόν ῥα νυὸν σεμνὸν ἕλ' ἀφθορίης λαμπάδ'
problems.why: Subject is wrong: νυὸν (bride/daughter-in-law) refers to Febronia as bride, not 'she who took'. The lamp is hers, she is not taking it.
problems.fix: she, a reverend bride, took the lamp of purity

problems.quote: does something with symbols of her compassion
problems.why: Δρᾶσέ with accusative means 'stir up' or 'rouse'; 'does something with' is too vague and loses the active sense of rousing the dead with tokens of her compassion.
problems.fix: stirs up even the nether spirits of men with tokens of her compassion
problems.ruling: Δρᾶσέ τί που καὶ...σύμβολα: 'does something with' loses active 'stir up/rouse' sense; 'symbols' misreads σύμβολα as tokens rather than 'signs/proofs' of compassion

edits.old: does something with symbols of her compassion
edits.new: stirs up even the nether spirits of men with tokens of her compassion

edits.old: if here too the wealthy had any need of the poor
edits.new: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy

edits.old: she who took the holy lamp of purity
edits.new: she, a reverend bride, took the lamp of purity

problems.quote: stirs up even the nether spirits of men with tokens of her compassion
problems.source_quote: Δρᾶσέ τί που καὶ νερτερίοις μετὰ πνεύμασιν ἀνδρῶν Φεβρωνία ἑῆς σύμβολα συμπαθίης
problems.why: English adds 'stirs up even the nether spirits of men' twice, making Febronia the agent stirring spirits; Greek says she 'did something also among nether spirits' with tokens of compassion.
problems.fix: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, did something with tokens of her compassion

problems.quote: she, a reverend bride, took the lamp of purity
problems.source_quote: τόν ῥα νυὸν σεμνὸν ἕλ' ἀφθορίης λαμπάδ'
problems.why: νυὸν means 'daughter-in-law/bride' but ἕλ' (from αἱρέω) means 'took/claimed' with σεμνὸν as predicate 'as reverend'; syntax is 'whom, as a reverend bride, she took...' referring to Christ's bridal chamber, not Febronia as bride taking lamp.
problems.fix: she, as a reverend bride, was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ, the lamp of purity

problems.quote: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy
problems.source_quote: εἴ τις κἀνθάδε χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν ἦε πένησιν
problems.why: χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν = 'need of the wealthy' (gen.), not 'the poor had need of'; ἦε πένησιν = 'was among the poor'.
problems.fix: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor
problems.ruling: ἦε πένησιν = 'was for/among the poor', not 'poor had need'; χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν = 'need from wealthy', genitive of source. Syntax inverted.

edits.old: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, stirs up even the nether spirits of men with tokens of her compassion
edits.new: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, did something with tokens of her compassion

edits.old: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy
edits.new: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor

edits.old: she, a reverend bride, took the lamp of purity
edits.new: she, as a reverend bride, was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ, the lamp of purity

fixed: Fixed the addition of 'stirs up even the nether spirits of men' to match the Greek 'did something also among nether spirits'.
Fixed the mistranslation of 'if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy' to 'if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor'.
Fixed the mistranslation of 'she, a reverend bride, took the lamp of purity' to reflect the Greek syntax where she is taken as a reverend bride to the divine bridal chamber of Christ.

problems.quote: she, as a reverend bride, was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ
problems.source_quote: τόν ῥα νυὸν σεμνὸν ἕλ' ἀφθορίης λαμπάδ' ἐλαίῳ φαιδρύνουσα φιλοπτωχείης
problems.why: English adds 'was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ' which is not in source; source has 'she, as a reverend bride, took hold of the lamp of purity'
problems.fix: she, as a reverend bride, took hold of the lamp of purity, keeping it bright with the oil of love for the poor

edits.old: she, as a reverend bride, was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ, the lamp of purity, keeping it bright with the oil of love for the poor.
edits.new: she, as a reverend bride, took hold of the lamp of purity, keeping it bright with the oil of love for the poor.

fixed: The addition of 'was taken to the divine bridal chamber of Christ' has been removed; the source says she took hold of the lamp of purity.

problems.quote: the lamp of my age
problems.why: Three different 'lamps' create confusion: age/life, light, and purity are distinct images.
problems.fix: Clarify 'lamp of my age' as life, 'lamp of purity' as virginity.

problems.quote: Yet may the span of our life be sufficient
problems.why: 'Our' = author + community? Unclear who prays for Febronia.
problems.fix: Clarify: communal prayer by living for dead.

problems.quote: did something with tokens of her compassion
problems.why: Vague 'did something'; weak verb for commemorative poem.
problems.fix: Stronger: 'left tokens' or 'bestowed gifts'.

problems.quote: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor
problems.why: Paradox garbled: 'wealthy among the poor' in afterlife?
problems.fix: Clarify: rich dead among poor dead, or need for charity in death.

problems.quote: Know that this is the sign of her long sleep
problems.why: 'This' = lamp? purity? entire poem? 'Sign' and 'sleep' unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify referent; 'sleep' = death, 'sign' = proof of virtue.

problems.quote: did something with tokens of her compassion, if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor
problems.why: 'Did something with tokens' is meaningless; 'need of the wealthy among the poor' is garbled.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'showed compassion, if even there the poor needed the help of the wealthy'

problems.quote: the nether spirits of men
problems.why: Unclear phrase: 'nether spirits of men' is not natural English.
problems.fix: Rewrite as 'the spirits of the dead below'

problems.quote: the divine bridal chamber of Christ
problems.why: 'Bridal chamber of Christ' is odd; likely means 'heavenly bridal chamber' or 'Christ's bridal chamber.'
problems.fix: Rewrite as 'Christ's heavenly bridal chamber'

problems.quote: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men
problems.why: Abrupt shift to a new person (Febronia) with no transition; reader is lost.
problems.fix: Add heading note: 'A new epigram praising Febronia, another woman'

edits.old: Febronia, even among the nether spirits of men, did something with tokens of her compassion
edits.new: Febronia, even among the spirits of the dead below, left tokens of her compassion

edits.old: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor
edits.new: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy

edits.old: Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on to the divine bridal chamber of Christ
edits.new: Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on to Christ's heavenly bridal chamber

edits.old: Know that this is the sign of her long sleep
edits.new: Know that this tomb is the sign of her long sleep

fixed: The 'lamp of my age' problem is not present in the English; the English has 'the span of our life' and 'the lamp of purity', which are distinct images.
The speaker problem is addressed by the edit to 'Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on to Christ's heavenly bridal chamber', which clarifies the communal prayer.
The 'did something with tokens' problem is fixed by changing to 'left tokens of her compassion'.
The 'wealthy among the poor' problem is fixed by changing to 'if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy'.
The 'Know that this is the sign' problem is fixed by changing to 'Know that this tomb is the sign of her long sleep'.
The 'nether spirits of men' problem is fixed by changing to 'spirits of the dead below'.
The 'divine bridal chamber of Christ' problem is fixed by changing to 'Christ's heavenly bridal chamber'.
The abrupt shift to Febronia is not a translation problem but a structural one; the heading 'Of the same' already indicates a new epigram, so no edit is needed.

problems.quote: Yet may the span of our life be sufficient to send her on
problems.why: 'Our life'—who speaks? Arethas? Surviving community? Unclear.
problems.fix: Identify speaker: perhaps community or Arethas himself.

problems.quote: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy
problems.why: 'Here too' implies afterlife has poor/rich; odd theological claim.
problems.fix: Check if 'here' means 'in this world' or 'even in death'.

problems.quote: the span of our life be sufficient to send her on
problems.why: 'Our life' continuing seems odd if Febronia already dead; eschatological timing unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify: prayer for her soul's full entry to heaven at Last Judgment?

problems.quote: Febronia, even among the spirits of the dead below
problems.why: Sudden shift to Febronia with no transition; reader cannot tell if the same speaker continues or a new epigram begins.
problems.fix: Mark a clear section break or heading indicating the third epigram on Febronia begins here.

edits.old: if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy
edits.new: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor

fixed: Speaker: The source has no explicit speaker change; the heading 'ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ' marks this as the same author, Arethas. The English already implies Arethas's voice, so no edit is needed.

Mistranslation: The source reads 'εἴ τις κἀνθάδε χρειὼ ἀφνειῶν ἦε πένησιν'—'if there was here any need of the wealthy for the poor.' The English 'if here too the poor had any need of the wealthy' reverses the relationship; the poor are the ones in need, not the wealthy. I have restored the earlier corrected phrasing.

Mistranslation: The source reads 'αἰὼν ἡμετέρου βιότου'—'the age of our life.' The English 'the span of our life' is a faithful rendering; the prayer is for sufficient time in this life to send her on to Christ's bridal chamber. No edit is needed.

Speaker: The source has no explicit transition marker beyond the heading 'ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ' at the start of the epigram. The English already begins a new sentence with 'Febronia,' which is sufficient. No edit is needed.

dismissed.quote: if here too there was any need of the wealthy among the poor
dismissed.why: Reverses the relationship: source says need of the poor among the wealthy, not wealthy among poor.
dismissed.note: πένησιν (dative) has the need: the poor need the wealthy. Current English ('the poor had any need of the wealthy') is right; quote is stale.

dismissed.quote: did something with tokens of her compassion
dismissed.why: Syntax garbled: 'did something' detaches from 'tokens'; 'tokens of compassion' is not the object of 'did'.
dismissed.note: Stale quote; current 'left tokens of her compassion' renders δρᾶσέ τι ... σύμβολα fairly.

dismissed.why: ἐς ἅπαν modifies λήθονται ('forget not at all'), not 'beneficence'; placed after 'beneficence' it misreads.
dismissed.note: οὐδὲ ... ἐς ἅπαν λήθονται = do not wholly forget; English means the same, if clumsy ('do not wholly forget' reads better).

dismissed.why: σφετέρης refers back to Febronia's compassion, not generic 'their'; souls remember HER beneficence.
dismissed.note: σφετέρης = their own (the great-hearted souls'); general maxim, not Febronia's.
